summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue fell to INR145.8 crore (from INR148.2 crore) on West Asia disruptions, while gross margin rose to 41.9% and EBITDA margin was 14.8%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue declined year-on-year as late-March supply and port disruptions linked to the West Asia crisis pushed shipments into April, with management citing a 10-15% shift in volumes. Gross margin improved to 41.9% on a better product, customer and export/domestic mix, and EBITDA was INR21.6 crore (14.8%) with PAT of INR9.4 crore (6.4%). For FY26 revenue grew 9.4% to INR610.4 crore, but EBITDA margin compressed to 14.8% and PAT fell to INR35.6 crore from INR47.3 crore as new Khatalwada capacity and employee costs weighed. Management expects FY27 margins to be better than FY26 with H2 improvement, but Q1 faces a temporary margin hit as price increases of 20-25% are only partly accepted by customers (10-12%).

financial_highlights.change: vs INR148.2 crore in Q4 FY25 (decline)
up 9.4% from INR558.2 crore in FY25

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Europe about 58% of FY26 revenue, UK 12%, US 12%, India 17%. Domestic share is growing as a deliberate mix shift.

segments.name: Customers
segments.commentary: IKEA was 55% of Q4 FY26 revenue vs 57% in Q3 (management's Q4 FY25 comparison given as 57%). The second-largest customer was flat to slightly down YoY; the third-largest grew about 225%.

segments.name: Domestic / B2C
segments.commentary: B2C contributes about 14% currently, with a target of 22-25% in 1-1.5 years. All-Time branded domestic is about 15% of revenue within a domestic business of about 17%.

segments.name: Bamboo
segments.commentary: Pilot facility at Guwahati is shipping to customers. New 75,000 sq ft Madanpur (Guwahati) facility leased from May 2026 with 3,000 CBM first-phase capacity; capex about INR15 crore and maximum-utilisation revenue about INR60 crore. Commercial volumes expected from H2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 annual margins expected to be better than FY26, with improvement in H2 as sales rise and fixed costs are absorbed.

Gross margin and EBITDA margin targeted back to historical levels (about 18-19% EBITDA referenced by analyst; management said it aims to reach historical levels) with second half FY27 as the target window if conditions settle.
Annual capacity utilisation targeted at 70-75% for FY27 (FY26 weighted average 73%).

Installed capacity 39,000 TPA as of March 31, 2026, with about 2,000 MT under installation (to be added in June 2026) and a further 6,000 MT planned in FY27 (total 45,000 TPA; 52,500 TPA target held pending demand). Extra 5,500 MT procurement planned this year per management.
Price increases of 22-25% sought from base; customers absorbing 10-12%, with the 10-12% expected to hold long term. Q1 FY27 margin hit expected; pass-through for largest customer has an 8-week lag.
Management declined to give a timeline for INR1,000 crore revenue.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about 39,000 TPA across Daman, Silvassa and Khatalwada plants and over 170 injection moulding machines; Khatalwada expansion completed targeted March 2026.

About 2,000 MT under installation (expected to be added in May/June 2026); balance 4,000 MT of the 6,000 MT program to be completed through FY27; further expansion beyond that to be decided based on customer programmes.

Bamboo: lease for 75,000 sq ft Madanpur, Guwahati facility effective May 2026; first-phase capacity 3,000 cubic metres per annum; machinery ordered in full; primary board production at Madanpur and downstream finishing at Khatalwada (25% of expanded Khatalwada building allocated to bamboo finished goods).
Bamboo capex about INR15 crore for 3,000 CBM; expected revenue about INR60 crore at maximum utilisation.
demand_pricing: Order book described as decent; customers open to placing orders; management says no cancellations, only shipment deferments and no change in forecasts.
Q4 shortfall: shipments of about 10-15% of the quarter's volume moved to April; about INR3-5 crore of export orders delayed to April due to polymer shortages.
Raw material prices down about 10-15% (around 15%) from the war-driven peak; certain specialty grades sourced from Europe and Taiwan face supply constraints; recycled polymer sourced domestically.
Polymer volume processed was 26,300 MT in FY26 vs 26,230 MT in FY25; recycled polymer rose to 8,022 MT from 7,136 MT.

About 90% of export customers on FOB or FCA terms, so freight risk sits with customers. Dollar-linked export earnings give an 18-20% advantage from rupee depreciation, but the benefit is not passed on in the short term.
Management says Indian-rupee revenue from the largest customer and domestic business means the rupee benefit is limited there; Q1 price pass-through is still gradual.

qa_highlights.question: How much volume slipped from Q4 into Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said shifts of business starting in February moved to April, amounting to about 10-15% of quarterly volume, plus supply delays from late-March polymer shortages.

qa_highlights.question: Customer concentration and growth by client?
qa_highlights.answer: IKEA was 55% of Q4 FY26 revenue (57% in the comparable period). The second-largest customer was flat to slightly lower; the third-largest grew about 225%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a capacity expansion delay due to demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no cancellations, but expansion beyond the planned 6,000 MT depends on customer programmes and product mix; the company wants to see stability before investing further.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for gross and EBITDA margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin of 41.83% in Q4 is not sustainable at that level, but it expects historical margin levels to return in H2 FY27 as fixed cost is absorbed and mix improves.

qa_highlights.question: Price increase versus customer acceptance?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases sought are 22-25%; customers absorb 10-12% now and this is expected to be long-term. Pass-through lags by about 8 weeks, so Q1 margins will take a hit, which management acknowledged for about 15-20% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Bamboo revenue potential and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex about INR15 crore; revenue potential about INR60 crore at full utilisation of 3,000 CBM. Commercial volumes from H2 FY27; management declined to forecast FY27/FY28 run-rate.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 margin pressure: price increases of 22-25% sought vs 10-12% accepted, with an 8-week pass-through lag for the largest customer.
Supply chain: port disruptions at Nhava Sheva and Mundra holding material for about 10 days; specialty grades dependent on Europe and Taiwan.
Customer concentration: IKEA at 55% of Q4 revenue; the second-largest customer is flat to down.
Utilisation at 70-75% for FY27 depends on geopolitical stabilisation; management says it is still sceptical.
Employee and contract labour costs rising ahead of scale; management says the pace will be slower than FY26.
Bamboo ramp-up is untested commercially; revenue run-rate not guided.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term structure and pricing power but cautious on near-term visibility: management repeatedly qualified outlook with the geopolitical situation and declined to quantify FY27 revenue or bamboo run-rates. Explanations for the Q4 shortfall shifted between supply delays and customer timing, which left some analyst questions only partly answered.
key_quotes: So, the fourth quarter volumes have multiple effects. It is not just the supply chain.
We are looking at, trying to look at that our internal targets for the quarter are achieved properly in the next 40 days what we have for the quarter to end.
Margins, definitely, it will improve in H2. And it will be better than what it is in '25 - '26.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 margins better than FY26 with H2 improvement and utilisation of 70-75%, backed by 2,000 MT under installation and a 6,000 MT FY27 program, while phase 2 to 52,500 TPA is deferred pending demand; no explicit FY27 revenue growth figure was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides FY27 margins better than FY26's 14.8% EBITDA with H2 improvement as fixed costs are absorbed, but Q1 FY27 takes a hit as only 10-12% of the 22-25% price increase is accepted and the largest customer has an 8-week pass-through lag; Q4 gross margin of 41.8% is not sustainable per management.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q1 FY27 (2,000 MT in May/June 2026); balance 4,000 MT throug
rows.why: 2,000 MT under installation (about 5.1% of 39,000 TPA) comes live in May/June 2026, and the 6,000 MT FY27 programme (about 15.4% of capacity) is held, though phase 2 to 52,500 TPA is deferred pending demand.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Shipments of 10-15% of quarterly volume slipped into April and INR3-5 crore of export orders were delayed, with utilisation at 73% in FY26 and a FY27 target of 70-75%, so volume recovery depends on geopolitical stabilisation and no explicit revenue growth figure was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation averaged 73%, below the 80% threshold, and management deferred the step to 52,500 TPA until customer programmes firm up; the bamboo capex of about INR15 crore is already committed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to quantify FY27 revenue or a timeline for INR1,000 crore and remains sceptical on geopolitical visibility, with Q4 revenue down to INR145.8 crore from INR148.2 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 FY27 margins take a near-term hit from the 10-12% price acceptance versus 22-25% sought, applying to about 15-20% of revenue, and port disruptions hold material for about 10 days.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Bamboo commercial volumes from the Madanpur, Guwahati facility (3,000 CBM first phase, INR15 crore capex, about INR60 crore max revenue) are expected from H2 FY27, though the pilot is already shipping.

rows.label: Price increase pass-through: 22-25% sought, 10-12% accepted
rows.why: Customers are absorbing 10-12% now and management expects this to hold long term, with an 8-week lag for the largest customer, so the remaining gap to the 22-25% ask is the main margin swing factor.

rows.label: Order book decent, no cancellations, only shipment deferments
rows.why: Management reports no cancellations and no forecast changes, and the 10-15% of Q4 volume that slipped to April should flow through in Q1 FY27.

rows.label: Raw material prices down 10-15% from war-driven peak
rows.why: Polymer prices are about 15% below the peak, but specialty grades from Europe and Taiwan face supply constraints and the benefit is not yet passed through.
